title: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365: which settings does each user's Office get?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the policy paths, licensing statements, delivery behaviour and audit operations. The preview Graph call applies the setting in applyOnce mode, and the page correctly distinguishes its tenant-only scope from group-level controls.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: Policy scope is configured in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center through Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select Next. On the Choose the scope page

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for choosing a Cloud Policy configuration's user or group scope.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service group policy configuration scope priority automation API PowerShell Microsoft Graph; "Cloud Policy" "group-level" API scope. Opened overview-cloud-policy, utcm-copilot-resources and copilotPolicySetting; no scope-setting operation.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A policy configuration can target all users, specific Microsoft Entra groups or anonymous Office for the web users.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator can manage Cloud Policy and is Microsoft's recommended role.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.where: controls[1].ui; What to check: first bullet
claims.claim: Policy configuration priority is changed in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center through Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Reorder priority.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... To change the priority order for the policy configurations, select Reorder priority on the Policy configurations page.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for changing Cloud Policy configuration priority.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cloud Policy" "Reorder priority" API automation; Cloud Policy service group policy configuration scope priority automation API PowerShell Microsoft Graph. Read overview-cloud-policy and TCM resources; results documented UI priority or unrelated Intune operations.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Conflicting groups
claims.claim: The highest-priority policy setting wins when a user belongs to multiple targeted groups with conflicting settings.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied. The highest priority is applied

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Conflicting groups
claims.claim: Priority 0 is the highest Cloud Policy configuration priority.
claims.quote: The highest priority is applied, with "0" being the highest priority that you can assign.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; What to check: Pages and Notebooks setting
claims.claim: The Pages and Notebooks setting is reached through Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.where: controls[2].api
claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply a Pages and Notebooks desired-state baseline once when mode is applyOnce.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... Create a new configurationMonitor object ... or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risks and limits: Scripting is narrow; Open questions
claims.claim: The documented TCM Copilot resources and Graph route are preview functionality in Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: This article lists the Copilot resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risks and limits: Scripting is narrow; Open questions
claims.claim: TCM supports the Copilot Cloud Policy settings only in tenant-level policies, not group-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: Setting the monitor's mode to applyOnce makes it apply the desired-state baseline once.
claims.quote: An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive. Its result reports the outcome of the run.

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: A newly created configurationMonitor defaults to monitorOnly mode.
claims.quote: mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: The Pages and Notebooks baseline resource uses resourceType microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks.
claims.quote: "displayName": "Copilot Pages and Notebooks", "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "value": "1" }

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: The Pages and Notebooks baseline setting is carried by properties.value as a string.
claims.quote: The value property is a string, not a Boolean or a number. ... "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "value": "1" }

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: For the Pages and Notebooks resource, string value "0" disables the setting and "1" enables it.
claims.quote: Allows or prevents creating and viewing Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Copilot Actions. 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; What to check: code previews
claims.claim: The code previews setting is reached through Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: Select Customization ... Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. ... Choose the scope ... In Configure Settings ... Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages

claims.where: controls[3].api; Open questions: scripting code previews
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for this Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages code previews setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Enable code previews" "API" "Copilot"; "code previews" "CopilotPolicySettings" Graph PowerShell. Opened cpcn-admin-configuration, utcm-copilot-resources and copilotPolicySetting; none documents an operation for this setting.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Open questions: scripting code previews
claims.claim: The TCM Copilot resources reference lists no resource for the code previews setting as checked in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "code previews" "CopilotPolicySettings" Graph PowerShell; "Enable code previews" "API" "Copilot". Read the full utcm-copilot-resources reference: no code previews resource appears.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Cloud Policy enforces policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a user's device.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 lets you enforce policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a user's device

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Cloud Policy enforcement does not require the device to be domain joined or otherwise managed.
claims.quote: even if the device isn't domain joined or otherwise managed.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Policy settings roam with the signed-in Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise user rather than being machine-based.
claims.quote: When a user signs into Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a device, the policy settings roam to that device. ... Only user-based policy settings are available. Computer-based policy settings aren't available.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Governance controls: Access
claims.claim: Cloud Policy configurations are managed in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at config.office.com.
claims.quote: To create or edit policy configurations you must sign into the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. ... Commercial and US Government customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office.com

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: An administrator creates a policy configuration with a name, a scope and selected policy settings.
claims.quote: On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) ... On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps Click-to-Run service checks Cloud Policy for settings pertaining to the signed-in user.
claims.quote: The Click-to-Run service used by Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise checks in with the Cloud Policy service regularly to see if there are any policies that pertain to the signed in user.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Retrieved policies take effect the next time the user opens an Office app.
claims.quote: If there are, then the appropriate policies are applied and take effect the next time the user opens an Office app, such as Word or Excel.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings are available for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android devices.
claims.quote: Policy settings are available for devices running Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Not every Cloud Policy setting is available on every operating system.
claims.quote: although not all policy settings are available for all operating systems.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Some Cloud Policy settings apply to Office for the web.
claims.quote: You can also enforce some policy settings for Office for the web and Loop, both for guests who are signed in and for users who access documents anonymously.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Some Cloud Policy settings apply to Loop.
claims.quote: You can also enforce some policy settings for Office for the web and Loop

claims.where: What it is: What it governs; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Users, not devices
claims.claim: Cloud Policy provides only user-based settings, not computer-based settings.
claims.quote: Only user-based policy settings are available. Computer-based policy settings aren't available.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Cloud Policy automatically adds new user-based Office policy settings.
claims.quote: As new user-based policy settings are made available for Office, Cloud Policy automatically adds them.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Administrators do not need to download updated ADMX/ADML files for those new Cloud Policy settings.
claims.quote: There's no need to download updated Administrative Templates files (ADMX/ADML).

claims.where: What it is: Copilot settings
claims.claim: Microsoft's TCM reference describes 20 Copilot resources as Office Cloud Policy Service settings.
claims.quote: The 20 Copilot resources are Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS) settings.

claims.where: summary; controls[2].governs; What it is: Copilot settings
claims.claim: IT administrators control Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation and use through Cloud Policy settings.
claims.quote: IT administrators can control creation and use of Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Cloud Policy settings.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Not configured leaves Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation and integration available.
claims.quote: Not configured: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation and integration are available to the users.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Users whose organisation has disabled OneDrive creation cannot create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks regardless of the Cloud Policy setting.
claims.quote: If your organization disabled the creation of OneDrive, regardless of the setting noted here, these people in your organization can't create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Policy delivery is not instantaneous and uses group membership determined at check-in.
claims.quote: When the service receives the check-in call, Microsoft Entra group membership is determined for the user. ... the service returns the appropriate policy settings for the user and informs Click-to-Run to check back in 90 minutes.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Delay and restart; What to check: pilot
claims.claim: Office Cloud Policy changes generally require restarting an Office app.
claims.quote: Policies from Cloud Policy are applied only when the Office app is restarted. ... Some policies related to privacy controls will apply without restarting any Office apps.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Delay and restart
claims.claim: Some privacy-control policies apply without restarting Office apps.
claims.quote: Some policies related to privacy controls will apply without restarting any Office apps.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Delay and restart
claims.claim: On Windows, only the primary signed-in account's policies apply.
claims.quote: For Windows devices, policies are enforced based on the primary user that is signed into Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise. If there are multiple accounts signed in, only policies for the primary account are applied.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 subscription plans that include Microsoft 365 Apps.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 subscription plans that include Microsoft 365 Apps.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft tells administrators to consult their licensing documentation for specific Cloud Policy requirements.
claims.quote: Check your licensing documentation for specific requirements.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Cloud Policy does not support Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet.
claims.quote: The following plans are not supported: Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits: Users, not devices; What to check: groups
claims.claim: User objects targeted through Cloud Policy groups must be present in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra groups requirements ... Policies only apply to user objects. User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits: Users, not devices; What to check: groups
claims.claim: Targeted users must have a supported licence assigned to receive Cloud Policy settings.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned. ... Make sure the user is signed into Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise, activated it, and has a valid license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Cloud Policy overview page publishes no separate Cloud Policy price or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cloud Policy" "price" "meter"; Cloud Policy service advanced health reporting retirement replacement date price meter. Read the full overview-cloud-policy, including Licensing requirements: no separate service price or meter is stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The TCM resource reference states that Copilot Notebooks also require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks also require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Wrong product edition
claims.claim: Cloud Policy configurations cannot be applied to volume-licensed Click-to-Run Office versions such as Office LTSC Professional Plus 2021 or Office Standard 2019.
claims.quote: A policy configuration can't be applied to volume licensed versions of Office that use Click-to-Run, such as Office LTSC Professional Plus 2021 or Office Standard 2019.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Wrong product edition
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Apps for business supports only Cloud Policy settings related to privacy controls.
claims.quote: You can create a policy configuration for Microsoft 365 Apps for business, but only policy settings related to privacy controls are supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Users, not devices
claims.claim: Device objects in a Cloud Policy target group are ignored.
claims.quote: A group might contain both device objects and user objects, but the device objects are ignored.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Delay and restart; What to check: pilot
claims.claim: The Copilot Pages policy documentation allows up to 90 minutes for a change to be reflected when policy configurations already existed.
claims.quote: If there were existing policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 90 minutes to be reflected.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Delay and restart; What to check: pilot
claims.claim: The Copilot Pages policy documentation allows up to 24 hours for a change to be reflected when no policy configurations previously existed.
claims.quote: If there were no policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 24 hours to be reflected.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Overrides Group Policy
claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take precedence over settings implemented through Group Policy on Windows Server.
claims.quote: policy settings implemented by using Cloud Policy take precedence over policy settings implemented by using Group Policy on Windows Server

claims.where: Risks and limits: Overrides Group Policy
claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take precedence over preference settings or locally applied policy settings.
claims.quote: taking precedence over preference settings or locally applied policy settings.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No health view
claims.claim: The Cloud Policy health status feature was retired in March 2022.
claims.quote: The health status feature was retired in the second half of March 2022.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No health view; Open questions: advanced health reporting
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no date for replacement advanced Cloud Policy health reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service advanced health reporting retirement replacement date price meter. Read overview-cloud-policy: "In the future (no known date at this time), we plan to provide advanced health reporting and compliance monitoring features for Cloud Policy."

claims.where: Open questions: advanced health reporting
claims.claim: Microsoft says it plans advanced health reporting for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: In the future (no known date at this time), we plan to provide advanced health reporting and compliance monitoring features for Cloud Policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scripting is narrow
claims.claim: Monitoring and applyOnce fail for a TCM Copilot resource when its target setting is configured in any group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Network
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Apps devices need access to the documented Cloud Policy endpoints, including *.config.office.com for commercial and GCC.
claims.quote: Devices running Microsoft 365 Apps require access to the following endpoints: ... Commercial and GCC | Microsoft 365 Apps admin center | ... *.config.office.com

claims.where: Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Security Administrator is a supported role for accessing and managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: You can use the following built-in Microsoft Entra roles for accessing and managing the feature: ... Security Administrator

claims.where: Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Global Administrator is also a supported role for accessing and managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: You can use the following built-in Microsoft Entra roles for accessing and managing the feature: ... Global Administrator

claims.where: Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for TCM remediation and applyOnce on Copilot settings.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.where: Governance controls: Access
claims.claim: Commercial and US Government customers can access the service in Microsoft Intune admin center through Apps > Policy > Policies for Office apps.
claims.quote: Commercial and US Government customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office.com or directly in the Microsoft Intune admin center, under Apps > Policy > Policies for Office apps.

claims.where: Governance controls: Access
claims.claim: GCC High customers use a separate Microsoft 365 Apps admin center address documented in the overview.
claims.quote: US Government Community (GCC) High customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office365.us

claims.where: Governance controls: Access
claims.claim: DoD customers use a separate Microsoft 365 Apps admin center address documented in the overview.
claims.quote: Department of Defense (DoD) customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.apps.mil

claims.where: summary; Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: Cloud Policy records policy configuration creation when auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked.

claims.where: Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: Cloud Policy records policy configuration deletion when auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations ... are tracked.

claims.where: Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: Cloud Policy records policy configuration updates when auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as ... modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings ... are tracked.

claims.where: Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: Cloud Policy records priority changes when auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled ... adjustments to priority order are tracked.

claims.where: Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: CreatedPolicyConfig is the audit operation for creating a Cloud Policy configuration.
claims.quote: Created policy configuration | CreatedPolicyConfig | A new policy configuration was created.

claims.where: Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: UpdatedPolicyConfigPriority is the audit operation for changing a Cloud Policy configuration's priority.
claims.quote: Updated policy configuration priority | UpdatedPolicyConfigPriority | The priority of a policy configuration was changed.

claims.where: Governance controls: To scope one group
claims.claim: Microsoft's subset-of-users pattern gives the targeted group a configuration with the desired value at priority 0.
claims.quote: Create Group A containing the users you want to enable the policy for. Assign the Cloud Policy to this group and set it to Enabled. ... Set the priority for Group A to a lower number (for example, priority 0)

claims.where: Governance controls: To scope one group
claims.claim: Microsoft's subset-of-users pattern gives All users an opposite-value configuration at priority 1.
claims.quote: Create Group B that includes All users. Assign the same Cloud Policy to this group and set it to Disabled. ... Group B (for example, priority 1).

claims.where: Governance controls: To scope one group
claims.claim: Microsoft's two-group pattern can disable the policy for the targeted group and enable it for everyone else by swapping Enabled and Disabled.
claims.quote: To do the reverse — disable the policy for a specific group and leave it enabled for everyone else — use the same two-group pattern with the Enabled and Disabled values swapped

claims.where: controls[3].governs; What to check: code previews
claims.claim: The code previews Cloud Policy setting controls whether Copilot runs AI-generated code previews in Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: For Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages ... Disabled: Copilot doesn't run code previews in Copilot Chat or Copilot Pages.
